sources.title: Daniel Arovas, Lecture Notes on Thermodynamics and Statistical Mechanics, complete lecture notes
sources.locator: Full lecture-note PDF and corresponding author chapter text inspected; thermodynamics §§2.2, 2.5, 2.6 and 2.9, including the ideal-gas entropy formula in §2.6.

contents.name: §2.2: zeroth law as transitivity of thermal equilibrium
contents.support: The source states transitivity of equilibrium. The local postulate narrows the relation to its specified thermal-contact family and does not infer an empirical thermometer map.

contents.name: §2.5–§2.6: entropy inequality, reversible equality, and entropy of an ideal gas
contents.support: The source tracks the total entropy change of a cyclic system and reservoirs and distinguishes reversible zero change from irreversible increase. The local postulate specifies endpoint scope and does not universalize every irreversible operation.

contents.name: §2.6: ideal-gas entropy difference and adiabatic examples
contents.support: The source derives the ideal-gas entropy form and calculates entropy changes for adiabatic free expansion and reversible adiabatic expansion. The local example applies the stated ideal-gas entropy formula to a separate, explicitly stipulated constant-load compression protocol.

contents.name: §2.9: entropy maximization and stability under permitted exchanges
contents.support: The source derives stationary exchange conditions at an entropy maximum. The local postulate makes the feasible set and attainment condition explicit and distinguishes global maxima from local or kinetically restricted preparations.

contents.name: §2.9: constrained local maximum versus global stable equilibrium
contents.support: The source presents entropy maximization as the stability criterion. The local toy model supplies a complete algebraic witness that a relative local maximum on a nonconvex feasible set can be below another feasible value; it makes no material-specific metastability claim.

contents.name: §2.2: diathermal contact and exchange constraints
contents.support: The chapter defines thermal contact by a wall that permits heat transfer while not moving or allowing particle transfer; the local definition states the declared boundary and allowed channels explicitly.

contents.name: §2.5: reversible paths are reversible only under additional process conditions
contents.support: The chapter requires a process that can run backward and distinguishes quasistatic behavior and friction; the local item expresses this through a typed reverse record and restoration of all declared auxiliaries.
